scenes.title: A bag with a limit
scenes.narration: Imagine choosing projects. Each project costs some resources and gives a reward. Our bag holds four units. A costs one and gives six. B costs two and gives ten. C costs three and gives twelve. You may choose each project once.
scenes.note: Budget 4. Maximize reward, not the number of projects.

scenes.title: What does the function return?
scenes.narration: Function of index and capacity returns the maximum reward using items from zero through that index, with at most that much capacity. Index tells us which item we are deciding about. Capacity tells us how much room remains.
scenes.note: The return value is a reward—not a weight or item count.

scenes.title: Enter func(2, 4)
scenes.narration: We enter function 2, 4. We can decide about item C. Every call has its own local answer. The parent waits until this call returns.
scenes.note: Each call owns its local variables.

scenes.title: First: skip C
scenes.narration: First we do not choose item C. Call function 1, 4. The index decreases, but the capacity stays the same. This call must finish before we continue.
scenes.note: Skipping costs no capacity.

scenes.title: Enter func(1, 4)
scenes.narration: We enter function 1, 4. We can decide about item B. Every call has its own local answer. The parent waits until this call returns.
scenes.note: Each call owns its local variables.

scenes.title: First: skip B
scenes.narration: First we do not choose item B. Call function 0, 4. The index decreases, but the capacity stays the same. This call must finish before we continue.
scenes.note: Skipping costs no capacity.

scenes.title: Enter func(0, 4)
scenes.narration: We enter function 0, 4. We can decide about item A. Every call has its own local answer. The parent waits until this call returns.
scenes.note: Each call owns its local variables.

scenes.title: First: skip A
scenes.narration: First we do not choose item A. Call function -1, 4. The index decreases, but the capacity stays the same. This call must finish before we continue.
scenes.note: Skipping costs no capacity.

scenes.title: Enter func(-1, 4)
scenes.narration: We enter function -1, 4. There are no items left. Every call has its own local answer. The parent waits until this call returns.
scenes.note: Each call owns its local variables.

scenes.title: Base case: return 0
scenes.narration: The index is negative. There are no items left. Return zero reward. We check this before accessing any item array.
scenes.note: No remaining items → zero additional reward.

scenes.title: Skip branch returns 0
scenes.narration: The child returned 0. Store that reward in this call's local answer. It is the best result if we skip A. Now we check whether taking the item fits.
scenes.note: The child finishes. The waiting parent resumes.

scenes.title: Now: take A
scenes.narration: Item A fits. Its weight is 1. Subtract that from capacity 4, leaving 3. Solve the remaining smaller problem, then add this item's value 6. Index decreases so we cannot reuse this item.
scenes.note: Subtract weight. Add value. Move to the previous item.

scenes.title: Enter func(-1, 3)
scenes.narration: We enter function -1, 3. There are no items left. Every call has its own local answer. The parent waits until this call returns.

scenes.note: No remaining items → zero additional reward.

scenes.title: Compare 0 and 6
scenes.narration: The take child returned 0. Add value 6 to get 6. Skipping gives 0. Taking gives 6. Maximum chooses 6. These are two possibilities, not two items being added together.
scenes.note: Compare the complete rewards of the two branches.

scenes.title: Return 6 from func(0, 4)
scenes.narration: This call is finished. Return 6 to its parent. The parent receives a number, not the child's local variables.
scenes.note: A return goes back to the immediately waiting caller.

scenes.title: The answer: A + C
scenes.narration: The final maximum reward is 18. Choose A and C. Their total weight is four and their total value is eighteen. Skipping C gave sixteen. Taking C gave twelve plus six, which is eighteen.
scenes.note: 0/1 means each item is either taken once or not taken.

scenes.title: Why recursion becomes slow
scenes.narration: In the worst case every item has two choices, so plain recursion takes exponential time, O of two to the n. The recursion depth is at most n, so auxiliary stack space is O of n. Calls can repeat the same index and capacity. Memoization stores those answers, but that is a separate next concept.
scenes.note: Positive integer weights are assumed. No memoization in this approach.
